newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-BOWE-GOLOTA REMATCH SET FOR DECEMBER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BOWE-GOLOTA REMATCH SET FOR DECEMBER.

text.p: An agreement has been reached for a December 14 rematch between heavyweights Riddick Bowe and Poland's Andrew Golota, whose first bout exploded into a riot at Madison Square Garden, promoter Dino Duva announced on Saturday.
Duva, president of Main Events, did not give a location for the fight but said his company would be the sole promoter.

In their first fight on July 11, Bowe, despite trailing on all three judges' cards, emerged with a victory when Golota was disqualified late in the seventh round for repeated low blows. Cornermen for both fighters began brawling and the fight carried over to spectators at ringside.

Bowe's manager, Rock Newman, was banned from attending any New York fights until August 1, 1997, and his company Spencer Promotions, Inc, was fined $250,000 and banned from promoting boxing events in New York for the same period by the New York State Athletic Commission.
Jason Harris, a Bowe camp member who was caught on videotape attacking Golota with a cellular phone, also was permanently barred from any employment relationship with Spencer or Bowe.
"The controversy following the first fight almost obscured the fact that Andrew Golota stepped up, that night, to the ranks of the legitimate heavyweight contenders," Duva said in his announcement.
"Many people believe that, if not for the fouls, Golota would have won the fight."
Bowe, a former undisputed heavyweight champion, is 39-1. The Brooklyn, New York, native's only loss was a 12-round decision to Evander Holyfield in 1993.
Golota, born in Warsaw but now living in Chicago, stopped all but three of his first 28 pro opponents before the disqualification loss.
